ordered_diagnoses: Spinal cord compression due to metastatic tumor

facts.raw_span: A 50-year-old man
no significant past medical history
1-week history of rapidly progressive gait disturbance
no back pain, fevers, night sweats, or weight loss
full strength throughout all extremities
decreased sensation from the T3 dermatome downward
four beats of clonus bilaterally
hyperreflexia in the lower extremities
profound ataxia, rendering him unable to walk more than a few steps
Contrast-enhanced MRI of the thoracic spine demonstrated a diffusely enhancing lesion centered at T1 with near-circumferential epidural extension causing severe cord compression
CT of the thoracic spine showed an expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body with extension into the left pedicle and posterior elements
CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis revealed no evidence of a primary malignancy

support_spans: profound ataxia, rendering him unable to walk more than a few steps

contradict_spans: no back pain, fevers, night sweats, or weight loss
concepts.why: The patient's rapidly progressive neurological decline and the MRI findings of a diffusely enhancing lesion with epidural extension are consistent with a spinal epidural abscess, although the lack of systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss is atypical.

support_spans: CT of the thoracic spine showed an expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body with extension into the left pedicle and posterior elements
CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis revealed no evidence of a primary malignancy
concepts.why: The patient's spinal lesion and the lack of evidence of a primary malignancy elsewhere in the body are consistent with a primary spinal tumor, although the specific type and nature of the tumor are unclear.
